output.name: Skeru — the Asking Raven
output.myth:
Skeru sat on the highest stake of Hesk's Reel and put questions to the wind all day. Is the herring running? Is the goat-boy home? Where does the string end? Tavo heard her. He laughs at everything, so he plucked the questions off her beak and flung them out over the cliffs. Some came back as weather. That is why old women who ask the sky too often get answers, and why the answers are cold.

Above her the Gull That Stays keeps watch from the north, and she carries down any question the raven drops. Where does the string end? Skeru still wants to know. The answer hangs from the tail of the Sun-Kite, out to the south-east, the last of Aun's cut string, sewn to old sailcloth by Ennu.

Aun asked her once, the same thing. She gave him no reply, only a black wing lifted toward the Upper Sea. She is still up there with her wings open, asking.

Mend your nets. When you ask the wind, ask once.
output.finding: Find the Gull That Stays in the north, then go one hand-span (about 20°) south of it to reach Skeru, the black raven on the Windward Reach.
